clue.text: Sternutation at first — go away!

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, the first number
shoo is the cry used to send someone or something away

explanation.surface: A sneeze comes first, followed by a cry telling someone to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sternutation' is the formal word for sneezing; the answer is the sound of a sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternutation is the act of sneezing, and this is the conventional written noise of a sneeze.

clue.text: Tory faithful's trouble: that's with Europe — no love

annotationWithheld.why: 'Tory faithful's trouble: that's with Europe — no love (4,4)': TROUBLE less O plus EU only gives the letters if rearranged, and no word but 'trouble' itself (already the fodder) can signal the anagram, so one word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Tory faithful's trouble: that's with Europe — no love

clue.text: House briefly licensed …

parts.note: a pub is a ... house, a licensed drinking house

indicators.note: briefly means the word licensed is cut short, keeping only its opening

explanation.surface: A drinking house, abbreviated, holds a licence; the dots lead into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims 'licensed' to LIC. The whole clue also defines: a 'public' is a short name for a public house, which is licensed.
explanation.definitionFit: Public is a clipped form of public house, the licensed premises selling alcohol, so the whole phrase points to it.

clue.text: … to which appealing, pumps oil out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of pumps oil are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the pub scene, someone appeals to the drinkers while pumps push oil out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads on from 3-down: 'public … to which appealing' is politics that courts ordinary people. 'out' signals the anagram of PUMPS OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Populism is the political style of appealing directly to ordinary people rather than elites.

clue.text: Take off statute book and ring again

definitions.meaning: to sound bells again, a peal being a ringing of bells

explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke it, and re-peal is to peal, or ring, once more.

clue.text: Playwright Henry provides jobs for the clergy

definitions.meaning: Henry ... was an English dramatist of the 1960s and 70s
a church benefice, a parish post with its income

explanation.definitionFit: Henry Livings wrote plays such as Eh?, and a living is a benefice held by a parish priest.

clue.text: Prize sheep get going

parts.note: prize as an adjective means top or outstanding, a star
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: An award-winning ram is set in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To start up is to begin running, as a machine or a business does.

clue.text: Unconventional country half-swallowed by snake

indicators.note: being swallowed means going inside, so one piece sits within the snake

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
hemi- is the Greek prefix for half

explanation.surface: Some odd land is partly gulped down by a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia is a historical country in central Europe, and the name also denotes an unconventional artistic community.

clue.text: Review in Le Soir left out points made by desks

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
left out says the letter for left is removed from Le Soir

parts.note: the name of a French-language newspaper, taken as letters
a crit is a critical review
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A critique in a Belgian newspaper makes points about some writing desks.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Soir is a Belgian daily; 'left out' drops its L, leaving ESOIR, and 'in' sets the review inside that. 'made by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk with drawers and a flap, so the plural fits desks.

clue.text: One who is posh, too

parts.note: a means one
a swell is a fashionable, upper-class person

explanation.surface: Someone describes a person who is smart and upper-class as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole clue as 'one who is posh' = A SWELL, then the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As well and too are interchangeable adverbs meaning also or in addition.

clue.text: 16 in French not finished often by Irish

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter of the French word is dropped

parts.note: in French, often is souvent

explanation.surface: Something in French left unfinished, frequently by an Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in French' tells you to translate 'often'; 'by' is a link. 16 is the answer to 16-down, a reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir is a keepsake kept to recall a place or event, an aid to memory.

clue.text: Head of parrot?

definitions.meaning: an old word for the top of the head, as in ... tax, a tax per head
..., like Polly, is a traditional pet name for a parrot

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the crown of the head and is also a stock name for a pet parrot.

clue.text: Transport homework containing round piece of wood for study of 21

parts.note: a car is a means of transport

indicators.note: containing means the homework abbreviation holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on one's own home
O is round in shape
a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: Some transport and a home project involving a round wooden piece, for a course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is 21-down, hearts, so the definition is study of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiology is the medical specialty dealing with the heart and its disorders.

clue.text: Skull, maybe, 11 to 3 25 12

parts.note: the answer to 11-across is a keepsake, which is what a memento is
the three answers make public opinion poll; MORI was a well-known British polling organisation

explanation.surface: A skull, perhaps, set against a string of cross-references.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. MORI (Market and Opinion Research International) ran British opinion polls.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento mori is an object such as a skull kept as a reminder of death.

clue.text: East — East, not North: North's part takes one down 10

parts.note: the Levant is the eastern Mediterranean region, the East

indicators.note: not tells you to remove the letter for north from the word for the east

parts.note: the Levant is the eastern Mediterranean region, the East
a part of the word North, the two letters in its middle

explanation.surface: Compass directions pile up confusingly before something takes one down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' strips the north letter from the Levant. 10 is 10-across, so a lift takes one down as well as up; the run of compass words is meant to bewilder.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevator, the American word for a lift, carries people downwards as well as upwards.

clue.text: Nudge concerning bodyguard?

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a minder is a bodyguard

explanation.surface: A prod about whether someone is a bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder is a prompt to jog someone's memory, a gentle nudge.

clue.text: Peer upset — one from the other place has time to get in first

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of Peer are rearranged

parts.note: to the House of Lords, 'the other place' is the Commons, whose members are MPs

explanation.surface: A lord is put out because a Commons member has managed to act before him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles PEER to PREE. Peers call the House of Commons 'the other place', so its member is an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To pre-empt is to act first so as to forestall someone else's action.

clue.text: Rival bird dead?

parts.note: an emu is a large flightless Australian bird
late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: A competitor wonders whether a bird has died.
explanation.definitionFit: To rival someone is to try to equal them, which is to imitate and match their achievements.

clue.text: Die after fall, invaded by excursionists

indicators.note: after places the word for dying behind the word for falling

parts.note: a trip is a stumble or fall
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: Someone dies after a fall, and the place is overrun by day trippers.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a place full of trippers, the day visitors on excursions.

clue.text: Very hot fastener inserted in lump of metal

indicators.note: inserted in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pig is a cast ingot of metal, as in pig iron
a pin is a fastener

explanation.surface: A hot pin is pushed into a metal ingot.
explanation.walkthrough: A pig is an oblong block of cast metal from a smelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping, as in piping hot, means so hot it hisses, extremely hot.

clue.text: Preside in court over Eliot's suit

parts.note: a judge presiding over a case hears it
T. S. are the initials of the poet T. S. Eliot

explanation.surface: A judge sits in court over the poet Eliot's lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places one piece above the other in this down entry. 'suit' looks like a lawsuit, but it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Girl from 8 could be heard to start 14

indicators.note: could be heard says the letters are taken by their sound

parts.note: the start of the 14-across answer, its first four letters, said as 'mee-mee'

explanation.surface: A Bohemian girl seems to launch a long cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is 8-across, Bohemia: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème, the opera of Parisian bohemians.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is the seamstress heroine of La Bohème, the opera set among Parisian bohemians.

clue.text: Preserve drink for 16

parts.note: to keep is to preserve
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Store a drink as a memento.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is an object kept in memory of someone or something, a reminder.

clue.text: Records of Anglo-Indian currency?

parts.note: the anna was a coin of British India, a sixteenth of a rupee
British money was pounds, shillings and pence, abbreviated L, S, D from Latin

explanation.surface: Some records concern the money of British India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anglo-Indian currency' gives both: the Indian ANNA and the British LS (librae and solidi, pounds and shillings). 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are historical records arranged year by year.

clue.text: View from work of 10 in 3 house

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: in places the digits inside the house

parts.note: with 3-down, public house, which is an inn
the number 10 read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: An opinion drawn from a piece about a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: '3 house' reads 3-down in front of 'house': a public house, an INN. The digits of 10 look like I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view one holds about something.

clue.text: Surprised comment good guy threw out

parts.note: ST, saint, stands for a good person

indicators.note: out means thrown into disorder, so the letters of threw are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark of surprise when a decent fellow got thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewth is an exclamation of surprise or dismay, a minced oath from 'God's truth'.
